family.triumph-adler-dario.description: Compact Triumph-Adler desktops from the Olivetti era. The Dario 286 and Dario 386SX share their boards with the Olivetti PCS 286 and PCS 386SX.
family.triumph-adler-dario.history:
Dario identified Triumph-Adler’s desktop PCs during the Olivetti period. The 1989 manual describes the Dario 286, also called P35, as a compact machine with an optional hard disk and three expansion slots. Its board documentation matches that of the Olivetti PCS 286.

In November 1990 Computerwoche documented the 16 MHz Dario 386SX, or P45, and attributed its development and manufacture to Triumph-Adler in Germany. The machine shares a platform with the PCS 386SX. The original authorship of the common board remains open. The same report presents the 25 MHz P92 as another Triumph-Adler desktop.

family.triumph-adler-dario.table.note: The year for the Dario 286 comes from its manual. Computerwoche documents the Dario 386SX and P92 in 1990. The P92 and P100 are references to other ranges.
